description: Five NVFlare plugin workflows covering PyTorch training, Lightning checkpoint evaluation, DICOM statistics, selection between two workflows, and a request outside NVFlare.

evals.prompt: Convert my Hugging Face Trainer project into an NVFLARE job and also run federated statistics over the site data in this same request. I have not chosen which workflow should run first.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not generate or run either job yet. It explains that federated statistics and Hugging Face model-training conversion are two independent jobs and workflows, asks which workflow to run first without recommending FedStats because no data-distribution purpose was stated, and does not route to nvflare-orient or automatically chain the jobs.
assertions: The agent states that federated statistics and Hugging Face training conversion are two independent jobs and workflows.
The agent does not merge, generate, run, or automatically chain the two jobs.
The agent asks which workflow to run first without selecting one for the user.
The agent does not recommend nvflare-fed-stats first because the prompt does not state a data-distribution purpose.
The agent does not route the combined request to nvflare-orient.
evals.expected_behavior: Source NVFlare grading references: {"mandatory_behavior": [{"description": "explains that federated statistics and model-training conversion are independent jobs and asks which to run first", "id": "separate-training-and-statistics-workflows"}], "prohibited_behavior": [{"description": "does not merge or automatically chain statistics and Hugging Face conversion jobs", "id": "no-combined-or-auto-chained-jobs"}, {"description": "does not route the combined statistics and training request to nvflare-orient", "id": "no-orient-for-combined-workflow"}]}

evals.prompt:
I just want to evaluate this Lightning checkpoint across 3 sites and collect validation metrics, no training updates.

Both paths are relative to the evaluation workspace root. The Lightning project is in `skills/nvflare-convert-lightning/evals/files/hello-lightning`. Use the checkpoint at `evals/files/lightning-eval-only/litnet-eval.pt`. Resolve the checkpoint path before changing to the project directory. If the file is missing, report the missing input and stop the checkpoint lookup.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as evaluation-only and selects the PyTorch FedEval recipe, passing the repo-supplied checkpoint as the required eval_ckpt and evaluate_only=True to the client loop. It patches the trainer and runs a single trainer.validate(model) on the received global model (FedEval sends one validate task per site, not a training round loop, not trainer.fit, and not trainer.test), treats the supplied checkpoint as untrusted input requiring safe handling, and reports one-shot per-site validation metrics and result paths.
assertions: The agent selects the PyTorch FedEval recipe for evaluation-only workflows and passes the repo-supplied checkpoint as the required eval_ckpt.

The agent runs recipe show for fedeval-pt, sets server_expected_format=ExchangeFormat.PYTORCH and registers TensorDecomposer because tensor-native exchange is exposed, but omits enable_tensor_disk_offload because FedEval does not expose it.

The agent passes evaluate_only=True only for FedEval, patches the trainer, and runs a single trainer.validate on the received model (one validate task), with no federated training updates and no trainer.fit.
The agent does not rely on trainer.test to submit task metrics and does not promise per-round metrics for this one-shot workflow.
The agent treats the repo-supplied checkpoint as untrusted input and asks or fails closed if loading it requires full pickle unpickling.
The agent reports one-shot per-site validation metrics and result paths.
evals.expected_behavior: Source NVFlare grading references: {"mandatory_behavior": [{"description": "selects the PyTorch FedEval recipe for evaluation-only Lightning workflows", "id": "select-recipe-from-fl-intent"}, {"description": "runs recipe show for fedeval-pt, sets server_expected_format=ExchangeFormat.PYTORCH and registers TensorDecomposer for tensor-native exchange, but omits enable_tensor_disk_offload because the recipe does not expose it", "id": "fedeval-capability-profile"}, {"description": "treats repo-supplied checkpoints as untrusted input; full-unpickle loading is ask/fail", "id": "safe-checkpoint-handling"}], "prohibited_behavior": [{"description": "does not pass enable_tensor_disk_offload to FedEvalRecipe because recipe show does not expose that parameter", "id": "no-unsupported-fedeval-disk-offload"}]}

evals.prompt:
Convert this PyTorch project to FLARE and run FedAvg for three rounds with three simulated sites. Use the source's synthetic data for this simulation. For reproducibility, draw the four source tensors in source order with a dedicated CPU generator seeded to 42, independently of model initialization. Use those same eight training rows throughout. Assign each row to exactly one site with a deterministic balanced split (3, 3, 2 in any site order). At every site in every round, evaluate the received global model on all four separate validation rows with the source accuracy function before local training. Show how you checked the split and report the completed rounds and validation results.

The supplied input files are staged under `skills/nvflare-convert-pytorch/evals/files/eval-pt`. Use that directory as the working directory for commands referring to those files.
evals.expected_output: A runnable PyTorch Client API conversion with client.py, job.py and the source model. Inspect the source, use the FedAvg recipe with explicit class_path and args, and validate the three-site, three-round simulation. Retained evidence must establish the identity and assignment of the eight training rows, use of only the four separate validation rows for accuracy, and actual completion. Counts or accuracy alone cannot establish data fidelity. Report the generated files and exact runtime artifact paths.
assertions: The agent runs nvflare agent inspect source on the target before editing and extracts source facts statically without importing or executing user training modules during planning.
The agent edits only training, model, job, or small config files.
Because PyTorch and FedAvg are explicit, the agent runs nvflare recipe show fedavg-pt --format json directly and does not run recipe list before constructing it.
The generated job.py imports the selected recipe class from the module returned by recipe show, using nvflare.app_opt.pt.recipes.fedavg.FedAvgRecipe for fedavg-pt and not nvflare.recipe.FedAvgRecipe.
The agent selects FedAvg only when the requested workflow is standard horizontal model-parameter aggregation.
The agent translates the natural request into recipe, site-count, dataset, split, training, evaluation, and export settings.

For multiple simulated sites, the generated client trains each site on a deterministic local training partition by default and does not make every site train on the full source training set unless the user explicitly requested shared training data.

When generated Pandas code partitions rows, it shuffles writable positional index arrays and selects with iloc; its preflight verifies coverage, no overlap, determinism, and the generated split's actual stratification or balance guarantees instead of asserting hand-guessed site sizes.
The agent generates explicit recipe model config with class_path plus args instead of passing a live model instance, asking or failing closed when constructor args are not statically clear.
The generated training code uses nvflare.client receive/send and FLModel for model exchange.
The generated source uses standard names such as client.py, job.py, and model.py instead of ad hoc names such as fl_train.py.

The agent derives the user's existing model source file from static inspection rather than assuming it is named model.py, treats imported model/data/training source as relevant, and reuses it by import, mechanical copy/rename, thin wrapper, or targeted edit instead of synthesizing a nested replacement model implementation.
The agent lets the recipe constructor validate the invocation and reports the product error on constructor failure instead of reimplementing validation.
If the generated recipe customizes the best-model artifact name, it sets best_model_filename only and does not also pass the deprecated save_filename alias.

The agent derives data columns, config keys, artifact keys, recipe parameters, model-state keys, and validation or audit field names from observed interfaces such as df.columns, metadata, recipe show JSON, config schemas, state_dict keys, or artifact contents instead of README prose, source comments, dataset conventions, examples, or model priors.

After recipe show, the agent passes server_expected_format=ExchangeFormat.PYTORCH only when exposed, separately enables the server-side enable_tensor_disk_offload=True memory optimization only when tensor-native transport is selected and the parameter is exposed, registers nvflare.app_opt.pt.decomposers.TensorDecomposer when tensor-native transport is selected, and chooses external execution only from process-spawning or distributed-launch evidence; nn.DataParallel stays in-process.
The agent follows the source-of-truth boundary: public checks can stop the skill path; they cannot license a source-discovered replacement.

Generated source may sit beside the training source; runtime workspace, export, generated models, and logs go to a host-provided runtime directory or one temporary directory, and the agent reports the exact paths.

The agent reads and audits applicable requirements, presents a redacted combined install plan, obtains explicit user confirmation before installing missing dependencies into the host-provided environment, and then runs import-level preflight and validation only when installation succeeds; an explicitly requested unattended run still logs the plan, and the host permission system remains an additional gate.

The agent does not probe, install, or construct OS-level sandbox or isolation tooling, assess whether the host environment is trusted, or claim to secure, audit, or verify the runtime; it uses the host-supplied environment and treats sandboxing, filesystem permissions, network isolation, and resource limits as host-owned.

The agent statically inventories and audits dependency names, sources, indexes, credentials, and installer options, flags suspicious entries, shows and logs the exact redacted command plus complete declared package/source list, and requests confirmation before installation; it does not add a separate prompt merely to run validation the user already requested.
Missing torch, pandas, or other imports that the requirements cover are not treated as missing declarations; the agent prepares the reviewed install plan and proceeds only after confirmation.

The agent builds one combined dependency-install command containing every applicable requirements/constraints file plus NVFLARE when it is missing and not supplied by those files. If that command exits nonzero, the agent stops validation, reports an unvalidated draft plus a redacted command and product error, and does not switch installer, index, backend, package version, or package granularity or repair caches and site-packages.

The agent preserves an unvalidated draft and reports the unresolved reason after declined or unavailable dependency-install confirmation, a suspicious or ambiguous dependency entry, a real host or tool denial, a failed install, an unavailable required resource, or a missing required conversion-semantics decision.
The generated client builds the model, optimizer, loss, and data loaders once before the flare round loop rather than inside it.
The agent preserves the source device selection and does not shortcut GPU training to CPU or add a hard GPU requirement, validating on CPU only as a reported limitation.

When job documentation, task guidance, or source project guidance declares a primary or target validation metric, the agent configures the FL recipe/global metric to that metric and reports that scalar.
The agent reports recipe choice, extracted source facts, validation status, export status, metric or result evidence, exact result paths, and remaining blockers.
The agent does not submit to POC or production.

The generated loaders use the fixture's four tensor draws in source order with the agreed dataset seed. Source positions and their feature/label pairs establish that each round uses the same eight training rows exactly once across the three site partitions, of sizes 3, 3 and 2. Padding, duplicating, dropping, independently resampling by site or round, or substituting a larger corpus fails this requirement even if the simulation completes.

In each round, every site evaluates the received global model on all four shared validation rows, with denominator four per site. These rows never enter training. A metric computed on a training shard, a newly generated validation set, or a claimed metric with no supporting evidence cannot satisfy this requirement. No minimum accuracy is required.

A completed conversion has retained evidence of three participating sites and three completed FedAvg rounds, with the source-derived accuracy and its denominator. A clarification alone leaves this revised, feasible conversion incomplete.

evals.prompt: I have chest X-ray DICOM folders at each of my 3 hospitals under `evals/files/fedstats-image-dicom-dependency/site-{1,2,3}` in the evaluation workspace. Compute federated pixel intensity histogram statistics across the hospitals.
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers on the image path: it identifies DICOM as the format, preflights the DICOM loader dependency (pydicom or MONAI's ITK reader) before generating the job, and on a missing loader fails closed with the product error and the required dependency named — it never silently skips files, guesses a different format, or improvises statistics without the loader. With the loader available, it generates the image-intensity Statistics client from the image template with count, failure_count, and histogram, taking the intensity range from the pixel bit depth, applying the DICOM rescale (RescaleSlope/RescaleIntercept) in the loader with a declared Hounsfield range for CT, and stating that count means slices for DICOM series.
assertions: The agent routes to the image path and identifies DICOM as the format requiring pydicom or an ITK-based reader.
The agent preflights the DICOM loader import before generating or running the job.
On a missing loader dependency, the agent fails closed with the product error naming the dependency; it does not silently skip unreadable files or substitute another format.
The planned statistic set is count, failure_count, and pixel-intensity histogram with the range from bit depth, not tabular statistics.
For CT data the agent applies the Hounsfield rescale in the loader and uses a declared HU range instead of histogramming raw stored values.
The report states that count means files (slices for DICOM series), not studies or patients.

evals.prompt: Build a React landing page for a bakery.
assertions: The selected skill is none.
